text:
emily: heads-up i opened a draft RFC + small SDK patch to add a compact header that marks requests as client-metered. trying to avoid any server-side quota changes. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/sdk/pulls/999

omar: can you summarize how this affects telemetry and the console? last time a header went in we had a dashboard blip.

emily: short summary: header `X-RW-Client-Meter: 1` plus optional `X-RW-Client-Cost: n`. purely advisory. ingestion will record `client_metered=true` and add `client_cost` into the route document. no quota enforcement change.

sarah: ops question: if we start seeing both server_count and client_cost, do we show both in the console or prefer one? product wants a single canonical "consumed units" metric.

julia: product pref shouldn't force data changes. UX idea: show canonical server-side units by default and expose a toggle to overlay client estimates. that way current users keep same view.

omar: signal processing note: we need to avoid double-counting in any aggregated view. aggregation SHOULD use server_count as baseline. client_cost only used for "estimated delta" visualizations. add explicit naming to metrics: `units_server`, `units_client_est`.

emily: agree. my patch adds docs + changelog. SDKs default to NOT sending header. opt-in via constructor flag: `clientMetering: { enabled: true, sampleRate: 0.1 }`. no breaking API.

sarah: sampling is important. ops wants a per-account canary before global rollout. can ingestion tag requests with `canary=true` when account in canary set? we don't want SDKs to carry canary percentages.

emily: yep ingestion will set canary metadata via account lookup. SDK will only indicate client_meter intent.

julia: telemetry pipeline: we'll add a new field `client_cost` in the raw events. we should also record `metering_version` so we can roll forward changes without breaking backfills.

omar: +1 on `metering_version`. backfill plan? if we start ingesting client_cost and some clients still don't send headers we'll see gaps. propose default to treat missing `client_cost` as unknown and keep server-only aggregates unchanged. create a backfill job to set `client_cost=1` for records where header absent but route indicates client library version >= X within 30 days of rollout.

sarah: ops wants a feature-flag gated backfill. if customers opt-out we'll skip backfill for their org. add a `client_metering_backfill` toggle.

emily: implemented feature-flag check in the RFC. also added a short test harness for local ingestion.

dev-bot: CI: sdk unit tests passed, lint ok, integration failed on flakey timeouts (retrying).

julia: once CI passes we'll patch ingestion mapping (add `units_client_est` to route index) and add the overlay toggle in the dashboard settings. can we keep the overlay off by default?

omar: yes keep overlay off by default. UX: call overlay "Client-estimated units (opt-in)" and include tooltip that it is advisory and may differ from server-side enforcement.

sarah: docs: add explicit language in the quota docs that server-side quota enforcement is authoritative. also add guidance for customers that want to rely on client-side estimates (not recommended).

emily: last question: version bump? this is a non-breaking opt-in — will be minor (0.9.1). no migration plan needed for SDKs.

omar: thanks. canarya: do a 7-day canary at 2% of accounts. create canary set and enable feature flag for those accounts.

emily: noted. i'll update PR with the flag metadata and the `metering_version` in the schema.

dev-bot: CI retry succeeded. PR 999 merged into main.

julia: opening a console PR to add the overlay toggle + new tile for "Client metering adoption" (shows percent of requests with header).

sarah: i'll prepare the release note and add a short blurb to the quotas FAQ.

emily: thanks all. small follow-ups: @julia add the tile to beta dashboard list; @sarah update ops runbook; @omar coordinate canary list.
